D.t: Juliana Stratton leads by 19.1 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 888,721 votes; a one point swing is about 23,253 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +10.0 and D +27.8. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +12.0. Your best recent poll is ActiVote at D +17.0; your worst is Public Policy Polling for Chicago News Weekly (D) at D +12.1. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cook, a projected net 937,670 votes; DuPage, a projected net 73,056 votes; Lake, a projected net 64,723 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Will, D +8.2, 5.6% of the vote; McHenry, D +1.6, 2.7% of the vote; Madison, R +4.0, 2.3% of the vote; Winnebago, D +2.5, 2.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Juliana Stratton runs furthest behind in Sangamon, McLean, Winnebago. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 75% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 64% of voters, 57 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.21 points; Voters without a degree, 57% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.83 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Juliana Stratton: Immigration voters 21 to 77, Small counties 33 to 65, Midsize counties 48 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.1M cash against $1.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
